label: early p / 1 input (p at step 0-1, 1 at step 1)
explanation: Fires almost only in the original and delimiter phases (99.5% of mass; essentially silent during copy). Core trigger is input p early in the sequence: p at t=0 always fires (precision 1.0), p at t=1 fires 58% of the time, and the rate falls steadily with position (23% at t=2, 6% by t=4). Input 1 at t=1 is a weaker second trigger (40%); 1 at t=0 never fires. These cover about half of steps and mass (dev F1 0.59). The rest of the mass is a diffuse tail: <DEL> steps (17.5% of mass, more likely in short sequences, highest examples after contexts like a l k / o w k), plus k, b, 3 and later p/1 inputs, made stronger by earlier tokens such as a, l, w, d, n, o. I could not capture this tail with a simple prefix-set predicate. The largest activations are actually on <DEL> or on a later p/1 after such contexts, not on p at t=0, so the predicate misses the top of the magnitude range. Does not fire on most other letters or digits 0/2, or on repeat occurrences (in_first=0 carries 8% of mass).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=0: p; t=1: p, 1, k, 3; t=2: p, 1, k, b) and the previous input (most: k, b, p, 2, 1, h; least: g, a, o, x); timing cues that raise it most: L=4 & t=3, L=3 & t=3, L=4 & t=4.
